mentl/6135c86:
The self-build ratchet's own next step, priced and refused.

The case for it is the strongest this loop has produced. Over ten iterations
I hand-read source to find what `mentl audit <file>` says in one command —
tightenables, iteration-shapes, drift shapes, unresolved comment refs, per-fn
rows — and ran the verb once, late, by accident. Every hand-read was a
confession. The obvious absorption is the PostToolUse drift-audit calling the
medium's own verb, so a finding arrives at the edit rather than at the commit.

The price refuses it. On the largest module, `mentl audit src/infer.mn` costs
4.91 s and 776964 KB; `tools/drift-audit.sh src/infer.mn` costs 0.07 s and
3780 KB. Seventy times the wall, two hundred times the memory, per edit — and
the memory floor is the one the concurrency gate guards.

The cost is not inherent, which is the finding. The verb re-infers a
9,616-line module and its link from scratch every invocation while the bash
scan reads text. Nothing about auditing requires re-judging what was judged a
second ago; that is the IC cursor's domain and the cross-run half is
Hbeta.persist.module-image-cache.

So that peer is re-motivated and its docs undersold it. Band O carried it as
cross-run compile skip, a performance nicety. It is the gate on the medium
auditing its own construction at the moment of construction — which is
Hbeta.audit.carried-truth-projection's whole point and §0's "unsayable before
a line is written". Until the image persists, the wrong move can only be
caught at the commit by a bash proxy, which is exactly where this session's
drift was in fact caught.

The middle ground was checked: a per-span audit still infers the module, so
there is no cheaper question to ask.

No wheel change, so no march; the pin is unmoved at 567a96659693.

mentl/618dba9:
#152. parse_body brace-path called parse_block_expr_checked directly —
parsed only `{ ... }` and stopped, losing every trailing `~>`. The
non-brace path used parse_expr (which absorbs the chain via binop_loop);
#125 fixed that path, the brace path stayed pre-#125. `fn f() = { body }
~> h1 ~> h2 \n ~> h3 ~> h4` (src/backends/wasm.mn:407) left the `~>`
dangling → parse_primary TTildeGt → E_OrphanHandlerAttach. Seed
parser_fn.wat:319-341 is explicit: "route through parse_expr ALWAYS —
including the `{` case ... parse_block alone returns the BlockExpr and
loses every trailing `~>` (perform sites then fall to LConst(0))."

Fix: feed the parsed block into binop_loop(_, _, _, 1) so the brace
body becomes the LEFT operand of the pipe chain — `{ } ~> h1 ~> h2`
is ONE PipeExpr, identical to the non-brace path, while keeping the
brace-context diagnostics (E_RedundantBraces / E_MissingBracesMultiLine)
parse_block_expr_checked emits. Converges the diverged brace path to
the seed canonical. Anti-drift-9/4 (restores the canonical
~>-chain-as-capability-stack, no deferral, no nested handle).

Empirical: pass-2 1981 fns valid WASM (no regression). P1 multi-line
{ } ~> h ~> h \n ~> h clean; P2 plain brace body clean (no regression).
pass-3 parse errors 1868 → 1854; first divergence advances input 407 →
535 (lambda (x) => body in call-arg position — next handle).

clob/615e139:
Every write-subcommand now emits a TOML sidecar `<output>.manifest.toml`
capturing the conditions that produced the artifact: kernel version,
git commit (via build.rs → CLOB_GIT_COMMIT), root seed (when
applicable), subcommand name, full CLI args, UTC timestamp, and a
sha256 of every named input file (model, corpus, tokenizer, confidence
head, etc.). The manifest lets downstream commands verify "the model
you're loading was produced from the corpus you think it was" rather
than trusting filename conventions.

Phase H adds:

- Cargo.toml gains `toml = "0.8"` and `sha2 = "0.10"`. Both small,
  broadly used, tree-compatible.
- build.rs runs `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` at compile time and
  exports CLOB_GIT_COMMIT via rustc-env. Falls back to "unknown"
  outside a git repo.
- src/util/sha.rs — thin sha2 wrapper. `hash_file(path)` returns
  `Option<String>`; missing files yield None so manifests can record
  `null`. Three unit tests including the known empty-bytes digest.
- src/config/manifest.rs — `RunManifest` with `new()` constructor
  (timestamps + version + git automatic), `with_seed()`,
  `with_input(name, path)` fluent builders, and `save_sidecar(output)`
  writing `<output>.manifest.toml`. `load_sidecar` reads one back.
  `cross_check` verifies recorded hashes against current file contents
  and returns CheckResult::{Ok, Mismatch, Missing, NoManifest} — wired
  in later when downstream commands consume sidecars. Four unit tests.
- Sidecar emission wired into cmd_synth, cmd_calibrate,
  cmd_calibrate_confidence (both head and meta files), and
  cmd_train_router.
- experiments/ convention: `scripts/new_experiment.sh <label>`
  scaffolds `experiments/YYYY-MM-DD_<label>/` with manifest.toml,
  run.sh executable stub, and notes.md template.
